# Connector-provider config (v1)

Schema for `.tera/connector-providers/<name>.hcl` config files. Each decodes to `pkg/config.ConnectorProviderBlock` declaring a KPP-backed out-of-process connector provider (ADR-059 Part 3) whose connector types register beside the natives. The block label is the provider name.

**Authoring a file here needs one kernel attribute set, and it is the only config kind that does.** Registering a provider EXECS the named binary, so a change to this directory reaches a running daemon only when `connector_provider_allow_exec = true` is set in the bootstrap HCL (ADR-122 D2). With it unset — the default — an add, edit or withdrawal here is refused on reload naming that attribute, the reload does not commit, and the running provider set stays exactly the set the daemon booted with; the repair is to put the file back, or to set the attribute and restart. Boot is unaffected either way: a provider declared in the configuration a daemon starts with registers at boot whatever the attribute says, because the operator who started the daemon chose that configuration. The attribute is kernel-only and restart-only for the reason every trust posture is — it bounds what a vault edit may grant.

| Identity regime | `inventory` — the block label is the identity; the file is a container and its stem carries no meaning (ADR-087 D3) |
| Current version | `v1` |
| Supported versions | `v1` |
| HCL block | `connector_provider` |
| Loader directory | `.tera/connector-providers/<name>.hcl` |

## Example

A minimal `connector-providers`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/connector-providers/example-connector-provider.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

connector_provider "example-connector-provider" {
  executable = "/opt/example/bin/example"
}
```
